source: Shi et al. (2023) Large Language Models Can Be Easily Distracted by Irrelevant Context
finding: Adding one irrelevant sentence to grade-school math problems (GSM-IC) sharply cut accuracy of code-davinci-002 and text-davinci-003 under every prompting method. This is the late-selection failure: the irrelevant input is fully processed and leaks into the answer.
numbers: GSM-IC-4K (4,000 sampled problems). Macro accuracy (a base problem counts only if solved under every distractor variant) was under 30% for the models.
quote: fewer than 30% of the base problems are consistently solved after adding distractors
limits: Only OpenAI GPT-3 era models. One distractor sentence inserted before the question. Newer models were not tested.
agent_relevance: Irrelevant tool output or retrieved text in the agent context is not filtered for free. Plan an explicit filter step, not trust in the model.

source: Shi et al. (2023) Large Language Models Can Be Easily Distracted by Irrelevant Context
finding: The kind of distractor matters. Sentences on the same topic, or with role overlap, hurt most. Role-overlap distractors drove text-davinci-003 macro accuracy to 0 on problems with more than 2 reasoning steps.
numbers: text-davinci-003 macro accuracy 0 on role-overlap distractors, problems with >2 steps (Table 4). Least-to-most prompting (LTM) gave about double the CoT macro accuracy on code-davinci-002 but a lower macro accuracy than CoT on text-davinci-003.
limits: Result for one model pair. Hard to compare across prompting methods.
agent_relevance: Distractors close in topic or role to the task are the dangerous ones, like the semantically related unattended message in Treisman's attenuation view. Filter on relevance to the question, not on topic.

source: Shi et al. (2023) Large Language Models Can Be Easily Distracted by Irrelevant Context
finding: Self-consistency (majority vote over 20 samples) reduced distractibility. The right answer was almost always among the 20 samples, so the model can solve it but a single sample is often pulled off.
numbers: SC improved overall micro accuracy by more than 11 points; 0-CoT gain 35.5 points. Correct answer in the 20 samples for 99.7% of problems (CoT, LTM) and 96.5% (0-CoT). Best macro accuracy with SC only 45%.
quote: the best macro accuracy among all prompting techniques is only 45%
limits: Majority vote does not fix distractors that bias all samples the same way. Samples are not independent (guardrail G4).
agent_relevance: Sampling plus a code vote helps, but more than half of base problems still fail under some distractor. Use it with a filter, not instead of one.

source: Shi et al. (2023) Large Language Models Can Be Easily Distracted by Irrelevant Context
finding: Two cheap prompt fixes helped: exemplars that contain distractors, and the instruction 'Feel free to ignore irrelevant information given in the questions.' The ignore clause mattered; 'Solve grade school math problems.' alone did not.
numbers: Instruction with original exemplars reached performance comparable to or better than uninstructed prompting with distractor exemplars (CoT and LTM). Exemplars with distractors did not hurt original GSM8K.
limits: Exact gains are in Tables 5-7 of the paper; not copied here. Later work (c06) found an ignore instruction gave little gain for LLaMA-2-70B.
agent_relevance: Mixed evidence on the 'please ignore X' instruction: it is attenuation by request. Test it per model.

source: Weston and Sukhbaatar (2023) System 2 Attention (is something you might need too)
finding: System 2 Attention (S2A): first call regenerates the context keeping only relevant parts, second call answers from the regenerated context only. This is an explicit early-selection filter built from prompts, before the answer step.
numbers: LLaMA-2-70B-chat. Modified TriviaQA with opinions (200 prompts): factuality 62.8% to 80.3%. Longform argument generation: objectivity up 57.4%. GSM-IC (100 problems, 3 seeds) in-topic distractors: 51.7% to 61.3%.
limits: Judged by GPT-4 for QA. Small test sets. Original context is discarded, so a wrongly removed fact is lost; a variant that keeps the original was also tested.
agent_relevance: Direct template for our agent: a program-controlled 'regenerate context' step that drops unrelated material before reasoning. Matches the schema rule that the model fills a slot and code decides.

source: Weston and Sukhbaatar (2023) System 2 Attention (is something you might need too)
finding: Plain instruction to ignore the distractor ('instructed prompting') brought little gain on GSM-IC, while S2A did. Early removal beat attenuation-by-instruction.
numbers: Baseline well below Oracle (same prompt without distractor) for random distractors and further below for in-topic distractors; Instructed Prompting 'does not bring much improvement' (Figure 7). Zero-shot prompting used.
limits: Figure-level result; exact bar values not extracted. One model.
agent_relevance: Prefer removing text over telling the model to ignore it.

source: Liu et al. (2023) Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts
finding: Position of the relevant passage among distractor passages gives a U-shaped accuracy curve: best at start (primacy) and end (recency), worst in the middle. Like a serial-position effect, and a bias in what gets used.
numbers: Closed-book accuracy 35.0 / 31.5 / 56.1 / 56.0 / 48.3 / 48.2 for LongChat-13B, MPT-30B-Instruct, GPT-3.5, GPT-3.5-16K, Claude-1.3, Claude-1.3-100K; oracle 83.4 / 81.9 / 88.3 / 88.6 / 76.1 / 76.4. GPT-3.5 accuracy can drop by more than 20 points in the middle; in 20- and 30-document settings the worst case is below closed-book 56.1%.
quote: performance in 20- and 30-document settings is lower than performance without any input documents
limits: 2023 models. 10, 20, 30 documents.
agent_relevance: Putting a distractor-rich context in front of the model can be worse than giving no context. Place key evidence at the start or end, and cut documents.

source: Liu et al. (2023) Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts
finding: Extra documents barely help: reader accuracy saturates long before retriever recall does. More context means more unattended input that is still processed.
numbers: Using more than 20 retrieved documents raised reader accuracy only 1.5% for GPT-3.5-Turbo and 1% for Claude-1.3.
limits: Open-domain QA only.
agent_relevance: Cap the number of retrieved items in the loop; every extra item costs latency and adds little.

source: Liu et al. (2023) Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts
finding: Query-aware contextualization (query placed before and after the documents) did not fix multi-document QA but fixed synthetic key-value retrieval. The U shape appears only in large enough decoder models; 7B Llama-2 showed only recency bias.
numbers: Key-value retrieval: GPT-3.5-Turbo (16K) with query-aware contextualization reached perfect accuracy at 300 pairs, versus worst-case 45.6% without. Multi-doc QA: slight gain at the start, slight loss elsewhere. Flan-UL2 inside its 2,048-token window varied by only 1.9 points best to worst.
limits: Instruction tuning is not the cause: base MPT-30B also showed the U shape.
agent_relevance: Repeat the question after the context. Cheap and reliable for lookups.

source: Ye et al. (2025) Differential Transformer
finding: Argues standard softmax attention over-allocates weight to irrelevant context ('attention noise'). Differential attention subtracts two softmax maps to cancel common-mode noise. This is an architecture-level attenuation filter, not a prompt.
numbers: Multi-needle retrieval in 4K contexts: accuracy gap between DIFF Transformer and Transformer reaches 30 points at N=6 needles, R=2 retrieved. Also tested at 64K length (8 needles, 1 retrieved) and on hallucination in summarisation and QA. 3B-size models.
quote: Transformer tends to overallocate attention to irrelevant context
limits: Needs training from scratch; not usable on a frozen model. Authors' own comparison.
agent_relevance: We cannot change attention weights in a scaffold, so the lesson is only that distractor weight is a measured problem and cleaning input is the scaffold-level equivalent.

source: Yang et al. (2025) How Is LLM Reasoning Distracted by Irrelevant Context? An Analysis Using a Controlled Benchmark (GSM-DC)
finding: Synthetic benchmark where distractors are off-path nodes in a dependency graph, so reasoning path and arithmetic can be scored separately. Accuracy falls as distractor count rises, and distractors harm both path choice and arithmetic.
numbers: Six models. At reasoning depth 5, Grok-3-Beta step accuracy fell from 43% (1 distractor) to 19% (15); GPT-4.1 fell from 26% to 2%.
quote: LLMs are significantly sensitive to IC, affecting both reasoning path selection and arithmetic accuracy
limits: Synthetic problems; step accuracy is strict. Final-answer accuracy can look better by guessing.
agent_relevance: Distractors do not just add noise; they also corrupt correct sub-steps. Check steps, not only the final answer.

source: Yang et al. (2025) How Is LLM Reasoning Distracted by Irrelevant Context? An Analysis Using a Controlled Benchmark (GSM-DC)
finding: Training with strong distractors improved robustness in distribution and out of distribution. Step-wise tree search guided by a process reward model (PRM) gave further gains out of distribution.
numbers: PRM-guided beam search improved out-of-domain robustness by up to 6.29 points (Table 4 deltas +2.57 to +6.29).
limits: Requires training and a PRM; gains are for models trained on this synthetic data.
agent_relevance: A check that scores each step, as in our code-run checks, is the transferable part.

source: Benchmarking Humans and Machines on Complex Multilingual Speech Understanding Tasks (2025)
finding: Dichotic-style test of humans and speech LLMs: listeners attended to one of two overlapping speakers and answered questions on both. Humans showed a large attended-vs-unattended gap, larger in their native language. Models showed a small gap even when told to focus on one speaker.
numbers: 40 listeners (20 Hindi, 20 Kannada native). Human selective-attention gap about 32 points in Hindi and 36 in Kannada versus 12 in English (L2), Wilcoxon p<0.01. Model gap significantly smaller than human gap (rank-sum p<0.01).
quote: models are able to jointly attend to both the streams even when they are explicitly instructed
limits: Read speech, 3 minute trials, synthetic mixtures, Indian languages. Per-model table columns were hard to read from the PDF text, so only authors' summary statements are used.
agent_relevance: Models extract from the unattended stream almost in parallel. They do not filter early, so a distractor in the same input is read in full. The instruction 'focus only on the male/female speaker' was not enough.

source: Benchmarking Humans and Machines on Complex Multilingual Speech Understanding Tasks (2025)
finding: Closed models beat humans on the unattended speaker. The paper calls this a super-human ability, but it is also a failure of selection: instructions did not make the models ignore the other stream.
numbers: Closed (Gemini, GPT) models beat humans on unattended audio in 2-mixture, all languages (rank-sum p<<0.01). Three-speaker mixtures: models show limited attended-unattended difference. Open Audio-Flamingo-3 (7B) weak on Hindi and Kannada mixtures.
limits: Models were compared at one prompt only; no prompt variants.
agent_relevance: No early gate arises on its own. A late-selection machine needs an explicit tagging step to say which source an answer came from.

source: MUSI: Can Large Audio Language Models Ignore Multilingual Distractors? (2026)
finding: Cocktail-party test with 200 items (50 per domain). Models hear an English target dialogue mixed with a distractor in English, Spanish, Korean or Chinese and must answer from the target. Single-stream accuracy is high and mixed accuracy collapses.
numbers: Gemini-2.0-Flash single-stream 0.955 vs cocktail-party 0.242 at 0 dB. SNRs -10, -5, 0, +5, +10 dB; three option permutations per question. Six LALMs (four open, two closed). Four answer options, so chance is 0.25.
quote: single-stream understanding does not reliably transfer to source-grounded reasoning
limits: Speech is synthetic TTS with fixed speakers. Multiple choice.
agent_relevance: Failure is source attribution, not hearing: the model picks the wrong stream. In an agent loop, track provenance of every piece of input.

source: MUSI: Can Large Audio Language Models Ignore Multilingual Distractors? (2026)
finding: Source separation first (a two-stage early filter) reduced overlap but did not fix wrong-stream answers. Open models often trusted the distractor stream and were confident about it.
numbers: At 0 dB open-weight models selected the distractor stream on 21.5 to 41.0% of items, giving 0.016 accuracy with ECE 0.73. Target-selection ratios 59.0% Qwen2-Audio, 78.5% MERaLiON-2, 78.1% Audio-Flamingo-3, 68.9% Qwen2.5-Omni. Mis-selection persisted at +10 dB where separated SI-SDR exceeded 16 dB. Gemini-2.0-Flash separation reached 0.952 but its mixed score was the lowest.
limits: Separation used an external separator, not the LLM.
agent_relevance: A perfect early filter is not enough. After filtering, check which stream the model answered from.

source: MUSI: Can Large Audio Language Models Ignore Multilingual Distractors? (2026)
finding: Negative SNR shifts errors to distractor interference: the louder stream wins. Distractor language matters: Korean distractors gave least interference for open models.
numbers: Separated-target SI-SDR rose from 2.95 dB at -10 dB to 16.16 dB at +10 dB; WER fell from 0.251 to 0.066. Gemini-2.0-Flash cocktail accuracy with English distractor 0.955 vs 0.320 with Spanish at +5 dB.
limits: Language effect partly tied to separator quality (SI-SDR), not only the LLM.
agent_relevance: Physical salience (loudness here; position or length in text) can beat instruction. Do not trust salience as relevance.

source: Wang et al. (2026) Increasing Computation Resolves Conflicts in Vision Language Models
finding: Seven conflict paradigms (Stroop, Flanker and variants) on 47 VLMs. All showed congruency effects; larger models resolved conflict better. Large models went below chance on high-conflict incongruent trials; small models stayed at chance, like humans at short processing time.
numbers: 4,410 tasks, 47 VLMs. Larger models above chance on congruent trials, below chance on incongruent high-conflict ones. Authors say performance versus log parameter count mirrors the human forced-response time course.
limits: Large models' high-conflict ceiling does not fully recover to match low-conflict, unlike humans given enough time. Zero-shot VQA only.
agent_relevance: Flanker-style interference is a late-selection signature: the flanker is identified and then competes. More compute reduces it but not fully.

source: Hu et al. (2026) Conflict and Congruency Effects in Large Language Models: In-Weight and In-Context Competition in a Verbal Conflict Task
finding: Verbal-only Stroop-like task ('crayon task'). The prompt stem pulls toward a same-colour default; an in-context rule either agrees or conflicts. Six of seven models (Gemma-2-2B, six Pythia 410M-12B) showed strong congruency effects. Mechanistic analysis found a short-range pathway to a colour cue (congruent) and a long-range one to the rule prefix (incongruent).
numbers: Gemma-2-2B: 40 congruent and 40 incongruent prompts; mean delta probability 0.9644 congruent vs 0.5676 incongruent, difference 0.3968, 95% CI [0.3529, 0.4407], t(39)=18.28; accuracy 100% in both. Stem-only same-colour probability 0.4252. Pythia-2.8B was the exception.
limits: Small models only; transcoder analysis available for Gemma-2-2B only. Measures next-token probability, not full generation.
agent_relevance: An in-weight default competes with a rule given in context. Longer rule lists weaken the rule: keep rules short and near the point of use.

source: Hu et al. (2026) Conflict and Congruency Effects in Large Language Models: In-Weight and In-Context Competition in a Verbal Conflict Task
finding: Making the default stronger by fine-tuning hurt incongruent trials and helped congruent ones. Increasing the rule set from 2 to 5 clauses hurt only incongruent trials, mostly for middle clauses (lost-in-the-middle again).
numbers: Five-clause vs two-clause rule: incongruent delta probability fell 0.3039 (t=3.2171, p=0.002); congruent barely changed. Ablating attention to the satisfied-consequent token hit incongruent performance far more than congruent.
limits: Causal claims rest on ablations in a 2B model.
agent_relevance: Evidence that the in-context rule must beat a prior; long rule lists are risky when the prior points the other way.

source: Teker et al. (2026) Feature Competition and Its Representational Origins in Vision-Language Models: Evidence from the Stroop Paradigm
finding: VLMs show a persistent text-over-colour bias: when word and ink colour conflict they follow the word, even if told to report the colour. CLIP encodes word identity along stronger directions than ink colour.
numbers: CLIP on 23,338 Stroop images: word accuracy 99.5%, ink recognition 15.9%. Pseudoword condition: about 78% of CLIP responses matched ink. Qwen2-VL-7B-Instruct ink-colour accuracy on incongruent images: 31.1% with a long 'ignore the written word' instruction, 60.0% with a short instruction that does not mention the word. Kosmos-2 never reported ink colour; InstructBLIP reported ink 28.9%; BLIP-2 gave both cues on 31.1% of incongruent trials.
limits: Six generative VLMs, small scale; embedding steering tested only in CLIP.
agent_relevance: Telling the model to ignore a feature can backfire because it names it. Phrase the task positively and do not mention the distractor.

source: Zhang et al. (2026) Thinking in Cocktail Party: Chain-of-Thought and Reinforcement Learning for Target Speaker Automatic Speech Recognition
finding: Audio LLM transcribes one target speaker from a mixture. Fine-tuning on chain-of-thought data (describe the reference speech, count speakers, compare similarity, then pick the target) and then GRPO with a WER reward raised accuracy. This is an explicit reasoning scaffold applied to attention selection.
numbers: WER 4.84% on Libri2Mix and 12.23% on Libri3Mix after RL. CoT data cut WER by 21% (2-mix) and 16.2% (3-mix) versus the base model. Ablation: removing speaker similarity raised WER from 5.29% to 6.08% (2-mix) and 13.57% to 14.93% (3-mix).
limits: Trained model; needs reference speech of the target. LibriMix is clean read speech.
agent_relevance: A written selection step (who is the target, how similar) before the answer helps; the cue to select on (speaker similarity) mattered most.

source: Nguyen et al. (2026) From Speech to Interaction: Analyzing Multimodal Systems in Cocktail-Party Scenarios
finding: Analysis of CHiME-9 MCoRec systems. Three strategies: audio-visual target speech separation, better per-speaker recognition, and LLMs that group speakers into conversations. They fix different failure modes; overlap alone does not explain difficulty.
numbers: Best system up to 57% relative error reduction versus baseline. Speech overlap can reach 100%. Baseline clusters speakers by temporal overlap and turn-taking (agglomerative clustering).
limits: Competition systems with different setups.
agent_relevance: Combine a front-end selector with a back-end consistency check by an LLM. Conversation grouping is robust to noisy transcripts, so coarse cues can be enough.

source: Cohen, Dunbar and McClelland (1990) On the control of automatic processes: a parallel distributed processing account of the Stroop effect
finding: Classic neural-network model of Stroop: two pathways (colour naming, word reading) of unequal strength, with an attention control unit that boosts the task-relevant pathway. The older computational model of attentional selection.
numbers: Not extracted this session.
limits: Not opened; described only from c19 and c18, which cite it as the model with built-in attention control.
agent_relevance: Same design as a program-set gate that boosts one source; LLMs lack a built-in gate.

source: Mesgarani and Chang (2012) Selective cortical representation of attended speaker in multi-talker speech perception
finding: Neural recordings show the attended speaker dominates representation in auditory cortex; this underlies attention-decoding and target-speaker extraction systems.
numbers: Not extracted this session.
limits: Not opened; cited from memory. Verify before use.
agent_relevance: Engineering lineage for cocktail-party systems evaluated in c15 to c17.

source: Luo and Mesgarani (2019) Conv-TasNet: Surpassing ideal time-frequency magnitude masking for speech separation
finding: A time-domain separation network that became a standard front end for cocktail-party separation (an early-selection analogue in speech engineering).
numbers: Not extracted this session.
limits: Not opened; cited from memory. Verify before use.
agent_relevance: Separation as a cheap early filter before an LLM; but see c16 on wrong-stream confidence after separation.

source: Kamradt (2023) Needle in a Haystack - pressure testing LLMs
finding: Standard test that hides one fact at varying depth in long filler text. Used by c10 (Differential Transformer) as its multi-needle protocol.
numbers: Not extracted this session.
limits: Not opened; described from the citing paper c10.
agent_relevance: Basic check that the agent can retrieve against distractors.
